svg.title: Metadata-Driven or Plain Pipeline?
svg.desc: The decision starts by asking how many data objects share the same load shape. A single one-off load stays a plain pipeline. Many sources with the same shape justify a metadata-driven framework, but the follow-up question is where the metadata contract lives: alongside the pipeline as simple parameters and a variable library, or in an external governed store when volume and audit requirements grow. Many sources with genuinely different shapes should not be forced into one contract — that path leads to the config-explosion warning this framework is meant to avoid.

text.aria-label: How much scale and audit rigor is needed?

svg.text: How much scale and audit rigor is needed? — Second-order question once metadata-driven is justified: lightweight config vs. externalized governed contract.Metadata-Driven Frameworks in Microsoft Fabric

text.aria-label: How many sources, and do they share a load shape?

svg.text: How many sources, and do they share a load shape? — The root question: object count and shape similarity, not team size or budget, should drive this decision.Metadata-Driven Frameworks in Microsoft Fabric decision path — Is behavior configuration or code?, Can retries be idempotent?, Promote a versioned execution contract

text.title: Lightweight: pipeline parameters + variable library — Modest object count, modest audit needs: parameters and a variable library are enough contract.
Keep it a plain pipeline — One source, one-off shape: a plain parameterized pipeline is simpler and just as correct.
text.tspan: An Orders metadata row selects connector, target,
watermark, merge notebook, retry policy, and quality rules

text.aria-label: Anti-pattern: forcing mismatched shapes into one contract

svg.text: Anti-pattern: forcing mismatched shapes into one contract — Many sources, but genuinely different shapes: one contract trying to describe everything becomes the config-explosion failure.FAILURE MODES
Externalized: versioned contract + run ledger — Larger object count or real audit requirements: build the full metadata-driven framework.⚠ Mid-run configuration change
In Atlas: select a choice → inspect evidence → drill into inputs, processing, outputs, example, controls, and risks.
